This page is specific to R. It shows how the Tree View follows the Material UI [theme](https://mui.com/material-ui/customization/theming/), set with the [**muiMaterial**](https://felixluginbuhl.com/muiMaterial/) package. To style the parts of the items, see [Simple Tree View - Customization](simple-tree-view-customization.html#custom-styling).

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(muiTreeView)
library(muiMaterial)
```

```{r}
fns <- data.frame(
  package = c("muiMaterial", "muiMaterial", "muiMaterial", "muiCharts", "muiCharts", "reactRouter", "reactRouter", "reactRouter"),
  fn = c("Button", "TextField", "Drawer", "BarChart", "PieChart", "Route", "NavLink", "useParams")
)
fns$fn_id <- paste0(fns$package, "::", fns$fn)
fn_items <- asMuiTree(fns, levels = c("package", "fn"), levels_id = c("package", "fn_id"))
```

## Theme and dark mode

The tree view shares muiMaterial's MUI runtime, so a `muiMaterial::ThemeProvider()` applies to it. The selection, focus and checkbox colors follow the theme, including dark mode.

The items inherit their text color from their parent. Set `color = "text.primary"` on the surrounding container so that the text follows the theme too. Alternatively, place `CssBaseline()` inside the `ThemeProvider()` to apply the theme's colors to the whole page:

```{r}
ThemeProvider(
  theme = list(
    palette = list(
      mode = "dark",
      primary = list(main = "#9819d2")
    )
  ),
  Box(
    sx = list(p = 2, bgcolor = "background.default", color = "text.primary"),
    RichTreeView(
      items = fn_items,
      checkboxSelection = TRUE,
      multiSelect = TRUE,
      defaultExpandedItems = list("muiCharts"),
      defaultSelectedItems = list("muiCharts::BarChart", "muiCharts::PieChart")
    )
  )
)
```

## Theme values in `sx`

The `sx` argument accepts the theme values, such as the palette colors (`"primary.main"`, `"text.secondary"`, `"divider"`…) and the spacing units:

```{r}
RichTreeView(
  items = fn_items,
  sx = list(
    color = "primary.main",
    fontWeight = "bold",
    "& .MuiTreeItem-groupTransition" = list(color = "text.secondary", fontWeight = "normal")
  ),
  defaultExpandedItems = list("reactRouter")
)
```

## Bootstrap conflict

**muiTreeView** can conflict with the Bootstrap CSS framework, used by default in Shiny functions such as `shiny::fluidPage()` and friends.

Use `muiMaterial::muiMaterialPage()` and `muiMaterial::CssBaseline()` to avoid Bootstrap and get a normalized CSS. See the [**muiMaterial**](https://felixluginbuhl.com/muiMaterial/articles/bootstrap.html) docs for more information.

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- muiMaterialPage(
  CssBaseline(),
  RichTreeView(items = fn_items)
)

shinyApp(ui, function(input, output, session) {})
```

## Security notes

- `JS()` code runs in the browser of every visitor. Only pass fixed code to it; never build the string with `paste0()` or `glue()` from user input, URL parameters, files or databases. Put the data in the `items` (or other arguments) and read it inside the function, e.g. `getItemLabel = JS("(item) => item.name")`. To embed values computed from your own data, serialize them with `jsonlite::toJSON()`, which escapes them.
- Labels given as plain strings are escaped. Never wrap untrusted text in `HTML()`, which is rendered as markup.
- Values sent to Shiny come from the browser and can be forged: see [Shiny](shiny.html#security-notes).
